summary: The AnsiballZ wrapper now catches unhandled exceptions in Python modules and returns a structured result with optional traceback, so broad try/except blocks that call fail_json are unnecessary.
questions: Why did my module task show MODULE FAILURE in older Ansible?
Do I still need try/except around my whole Ansible module?
How are unhandled exceptions in Python modules reported in ansible-core 2.19?

answer_card.title: Unhandled module exceptions are now structured results
answer_card.answer_md:
Previously an unhandled exception in a Python module printed a traceback and exited, so the task showed a generic `MODULE FAILURE` plus raw output. Module authors often wrapped code in generic `try/except` just to call `fail_json`.

Now the **AnsiballZ wrapper** captures all unhandled exceptions and returns them as a structured module result, including the traceback when enabled on the controller. Those broad try/except blocks are no longer needed.
